sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Automotive Replacement Parts and Tuning Accessories

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17; Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 233.5 (Beneficial Ownership Registry); FINTRAC Guidelines

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: FINTRAC AML/CFT guidelines, OSFI prudential standards, OFAC SDN list, UN sanctions lists, and Quebec-specific PEP screening

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in French; bilingual names accepted provided French is dominant
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names that could mislead as to business nature
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit written appeal to the Registre des entreprises within 30 days of rejection notice, providing detailed grounds for reconsideration

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for retail operations if address is verifiable and not a pure mail drop
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk (under 5% for routine filings); targeted inspections possible only for compliance concerns

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and incorporation services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for Quebec corporate formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization and apostille (if foreign documents required)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 5, 27, 29, 44, 108, 110 and 129; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, art. 21; Regulation respecting the Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, r. 1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Direction du registre central des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (constitution / acte constitutif) filed under s. 5 of the QBCA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; articles may prescribe authorized capital without par value, and shares may be issued for cash, property or services in consideration fixed by the board. No escrow or mandatory capital deposit applies to ordinary incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the Corporation was incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (Québec); NOW THEREFORE, the board of directors resolves: 1. The issue, subscription and allotment of 100 common shares to the sole subscriber for the consideration stated in the share subscription agreement. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], Montréal, Québec, in accordance with s. 110 QBCA. 3. [Director Name] is appointed as President and Chief Executive Officer and [Officer Name] is appointed as Secretary-Treasurer, each with authority to open bank accounts and execute contracts. 4. The standard corporate by-laws are adopted and the directors and officers are authorized to effect all filings required by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Declaration and Corporate Name Availability Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Online Name Analysis Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name declaration through the REQ online portal indicating the proposed corporate name and activities. The REQ performs legal, linguistic and distinctiveness verification under the Charter of the French Language and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Reserve the name if available and retain the exclusivity confirmation for subsequent filing.
required_dossiers: Identification of the incorporator (name, date of birth and address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name declaration within 30 days; if the refusal is contested, request a review by the REQ or proceed with a numbered company name in Quebec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Signing of Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles on the QBCA prescribed form stating the corporate name, registered office address, share structure, restrictions and number or category of directors. Prepare a French or bilingual version with French prevailing, as required for Quebec corporate documents. Have the incorporator sign and initial each page, and prepare initial by-laws and director consents.
required_dossiers: French or bilingual articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ later queries the wording, file corrective articles or a corrective declaration; no new name analysis is needed if the corrected name remains substantially identical.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles with the Registraire des Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Online Filing and Payment Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REQ secure portal and complete the application for incorporation of a legal person. Attach the signed articles in PDF with digital signature where applicable, identify the incorporators, state the number of directors or first directors, and pay the prescribed filing and name-analysis fees using accepted payment methods. Submit and retain the electronic acknowledgement with the file number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is rejected for a formal defect, correct the filing within 30 days using the same file and pay the applicable administrative fee for legal publicity correction if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Registry Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Registre des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the REQ accepts the filing, the Enterprise Registrar issues a certificate of incorporation and enters the legal person in the enterprise register with a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Download the official extract from the register to evidence legal existence for banking, leasing, contracts and tax identification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error in name, date or registered office, apply for rectification of the register through the REQ's correction procedure and substantiate the clerical or factual error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; Revenu Québec; Canada Revenue Agency; CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting, adopt the first board resolution, issue share certificates and open the corporate bank account. Apply through the CRA Business Registration Online for the federal business number, and register with Revenu Québec for QST, payroll and employer contributions as applicable. If employees are hired, register the establishment with CNESST and maintain the required corporate records and minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax account registration is refused because of classification, provide a revised NAICS code and payroll description; corrections can be made through CRA and Revenu Québec within 90 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the activity is online retail of automotive replacement parts under ISIC 4791 / NAICS 441310 and does not require an industrial classification from the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating permit is required; registration with Registraire des entreprises and any municipal general business/occupancy permit suffice for online retail activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no industrial process, contaminant-emitting activity or hazardous waste generation; no environmental impact assessment or authorization is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to pure e-commerce retail. If warehousing later installs cooling systems or manages packaging waste, comply with municipal wastewater by-laws, refrigerant recovery obligations and the applicable municipal solid-waste collection rules; no VOC or process-water discharges are generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety attestation from the competent local municipal fire service for commercial occupancy under the Fire Safety Act; workplace health and safety registration with CNESST for employees; structural load inspection only if warehouse racking is installed; general municipal occupancy inspection for office/warehouse premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec; CRA My Business Account portal (canada.ca) and Revenu Québec Cl@t business portal (clat.revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Business Corporation incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act engaged in online auto-parts retail, obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) with CRA program accounts (GST/HST, payroll, corporate income tax) using Form RC1 or the My Business Account portal. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada must also complete the simplified CRA non-resident GST/HST registration. In parallel, register with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (RDQ) to obtain the Quebec Enterprise Registration Number (NEQ) and then file an application with Revenu Québec for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) account, using Form LM-1-V, including the NAICS activity 441310 (Automotive Parts and Accessories Retail).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Business Corporation is a separate taxpayer subject to federal corporate income tax under Part I of the Income Tax Act and Quebec corporate income tax under the Taxation Act; no flow-through treatment applies. In Quebec, the corporation is also liable for the QST as a dealer if taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style 'check-the-box' classification election; corporations are taxed at the entity level. Available statutory elections affecting indirect tax status include: the section 273 ETA election allowing closely related corporations to be treated as a single GST/HST registrant; the section 156 election under the Tax Administration Act for QST consolidated filing; and, for non-resident corporations, the section 216(1) ITA election to compute Canadian tax on certain rental or timber income. Hybrid mismatch elections may be available under Part XII.6 of the ITA for foreign-affiliate surplus accounts, but are not relevant to this retail e-commerce structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal VAT) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) (provincial VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 in taxable supplies made by the supplier in Canada (Quebec for QST) over the current and preceding four calendar quarters, known as the small-supplier threshold; for non-resident digital or remote sellers, the same $30,000 threshold applies on Canadian sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal or Quebec real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing clearance, API telemetry, or digital stamping mandate currently applies to automotive parts e-commerce. Electronic invoices are accepted if they contain all required GST/HST/QST disclosures and are accessible for CRA or Revenu Québec audit. Quebec permits the use of authorized electronic invoicing solutions, but no pre-clearance or government approval of each invoice is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% GST/HST/QST) applies to supplies of tangible personal property (auto parts and accessories) and to services made by a registrant where the property is exported by the supplier or delivered to a common carrier, forwarding agent, or an outbound mail service for direct delivery to a destination outside Canada, and the supplier obtains and retains evidence that the property was exported. Services are zero-rated if supplied to a non-resident person not necessarily based on the Canadian market, provided the service does not directly relate to Canadian real or corporeal moveable property. For Quebec QST, provincial zero-rating parallels the GST/HST export rules for actual shipments out of Quebec.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency) or Canada Customs Invoice / commercial invoice showing HS classification and export departure point
Bill of Lading / Waybill / Air Waybill issued by a common carrier evidencing shipment and foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate from a Canadian financial institution or foreign bank transfer advice proving foreign currency settlement and repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rated supplies retroactively within the normal period (four years for federal, three years for Quebec corporations, extended for wilful misrepresentation). Claiming zero-rating without proper export evidence attracts penalty under section 280.01 of the Excise Tax Act of 50% of the refund or credit claimed, plus unpaid GST/HST interest and arrears interest under section 280. The penalty for making a false statement or omission is 15% of the tax amount deemed collectible under subsection 281.1(1), and criminal charges under subsection 327(1) may be pursued for fraudulent evasion, subject to fines up to CAD $20,000 and imprisonment of up to five years. Revenu Québec imposes equivalent penalties under the Tax Administration Act, and both authorities may claw back input tax credits and demand immediate repayment of zero-rated export refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central bank); Department of Finance Canada and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administer currency and transaction reporting obligations. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange administration; the federal Exchange Control Act was repealed and currency controls are prohibited under the Currency Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar enjoys full de jure and de facto convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under IMF Article VIII. There are no exchange controls restricting the inflow or outflow of funds, and no prior government approval is required for profit remittance, dividend distributions, capital subscriptions, or trade settlements. Companies may convert CAD freely at commercial banks; however, cross-border transfers exceeding CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC, and remittances of earnings can be subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act unless reduced by treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed timeline for repatriating export receipts into CAD. Exporters may hold foreign-currency accounts, retain balances in USD or other denominations, and convert at flexible commercial rates. For statistical and customs purposes, export declarations (B13A / ACI) must be filed to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), but these are not currency or treasury controls.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for ancillary transaction clearing, but low suitability as primary treasury destination for a Quebec-registered corporation. Non-resident fintech EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, and Stripe Treasury are not chartered banks and cannot take deposits in Canada under the Bank Act. They must operate through registered Canadian Money Service Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC, and only through contractual payment distribution channels. Such rails may be used legally for inbound customer settlement (e.g., Stripe/PayPal payouts) or for low-value remittances, but should never hold material capital or regulatory escrow balances. For a robust cross-border treasury, a tier-1 Canadian bank account must be the primary financial institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian Schedule I banks, particularly in Quebec, normally require at least one director or a designated authorized signing officer to present physically at the branch for the corporate account opening interview. Remote onboarding is permitted in certain bank programs for non-resident directors, using live video verification and certified digital identity proofs, but physical presence remains the default expectation for foreign-owned e-commerce companies. A federal or Quebec-registered corporation with foreign directors must also file any necessary extra-provincial registration and provide notarized corporate documents, resolutions, and signed mandate agreements under Quebec civil law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex offshore beneficial ownership structure (multiple tiers or trust arrangements).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart, certified copies of the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC), Quebec Registraire des entreprises corporate extract, jurisdiction-of-incorporation certificates, charter documents, and source-of-funds disclosure for each natural person owning or controlling 25% or more of the shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce model relying on payment processors (Stripe/PayPal) with aggregated settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant agreements, processor payout statements, platform transaction logs, refund/chargeback policies and analytics, ISIC 4791 / NAICS 441310 industry classification, website inventory evidence, and a clean compliance history letter from the payment processors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket wire transfers to automotive parts suppliers abroad (e.g., United States, China, Taiwan).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreements, commercial invoices and bills of lading, customs declarations (ACE for US, CBSA for Canada), warehouse lease and inventory reports, names and UBO address of each supplier, and a bank reference letter confirming the supplier's own banking history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow financing from non-resident shareholders without a clear reinvestment purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription agreement, shareholder loan or capital injection deed, paid-up capital computation under the Canada Business Corporations Act and Quebec Companies Act, use-of-proceeds budget, and an audited or review engagement statement from a licensed CPA in Quebec.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from foreign shareholders shall be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the Canadian bank account using the bank's corporate ABA / CBIC routing code, with a clear beneficiary account stated as the Quebec operating treasury account. The purpose code should reflect 'capital subscription / paid-up capital' and the remitter must be the exact legal name of the shareholder. FINTRAC monitors electronic funds transfers above CAD 10,000; however, no exchange-control license is needed. To preserve tax attributes, the company should record the equity injection in its minute book, issue share certificates, and file the required federal and Quebec forms. For shareholder loans, execute a written loan agreement with arm's-length terms.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements to foreign auto-parts vendors will be executed primarily via SWIFT MT103 single-customer credit transfers for amounts below CAD 100,000 per invoice. For high-value or contractually large deliveries, a documentary commercial letter of credit (irrevocable, confirmed) should be issued through the Canadian bank with the overseas bank as advising or confirming bank. Also permissible are documentary collections (D/P or D/A) and bank guarantees/standby letters of credit where suppliers require additional assurance. The company shall apply Incoterms 2020 and include the relevant HS code, invoice refs, and shipping documentation to align with customs and AML review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CAD deliverable forward contracts (flat or rolling tenors) with a tier-1 Canadian bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to offshore CNY or RUB when settlement currency restrictions exist
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (XCCY) on floating-to-fixed basis for long-term USD/CAD funding
Vanilla foreign-exchange options (calls/puts) to hedge transaction exposure on large purchase invoices

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) — mandatory enterprise registry update of directors, registered office, Quebec establishments, and beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the corporation's registration in the Quebec enterprise register; fiscal year-end is not the reference date; online filing is required for regulated entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of CAD 183.08 (online) or CAD 220.60 (paper); failure to file for two consecutive years allows the Registrar to administratively dissolve the corporation after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (CBCA) — applicable only if the entity is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act and registered extra-provincially in Quebec; the Quebec Annual Declaration remains separately due
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the corporation's certificate of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 100; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers dissolution proceedings initiated by Corporations Canada.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Quebec CO-17 Corporation Tax Return — ancillary annual statutory filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; tax balance due 2 months after year-end (3 months for a qualified Canadian-controlled private corporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months), increased to 10% plus 2% per month for repeat failures; quarterly prescribed arrears interest applies to unpaid amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for a non-distributing (private) corporation; shareholders may annually pass an unanimous resolution to waive the appointment of an auditor. A statutory independent audit is compulsory if the corporation is a reporting issuer, if shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued shares request it, or if the articles or by-laws impose it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in the CPA Canada Handbook Part I (mandatory for reporting issuers); Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II) are electively applied by a private auto-parts e-commerce corporation; permanent and timing tax differences are tracked separately for T2 and CO-17 filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Quebec Annual Declaration requires annual confirmation of beneficial-owner data in the register of beneficial owners: every individual holding 25% or more of voting shares or exercising de facto control must be disclosed with name, date of birth, residence address, and control details. Any share transfer creating a new beneficial owner or any change in control triggers a separate update declaration to the REQ within 30 days (CAD 38.88 online). The updated internal beneficial-ownership register must remain available at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes of director and shareholder meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180–440 (CAD 250–600) typical annual range for a Quebec registered office and corporate maintenance agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,800–14,600 (CAD 12,000–20,000) for a full certified statutory audit; USD 2,200–5,100 (CAD 3,000–7,000) for a review engagement where shareholders waive the audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general corporate income tax rate: 15%. Quebec general corporate income tax rate: 11.5%. The combined general rate is 26.5%, before provincial allocation adjustments and applicable credits. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) may receive the federal small business rate of 9% on eligible active business income within the federal business limit; Quebec's small-business deduction can reduce the Quebec rate to 3.2% where its eligibility conditions are met. Retail corporations must assess Quebec's prescribed-hours and other eligibility tests; non-Canadian-controlled corporations generally cannot claim the CCPC federal small business deduction.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential incentives include the federal and Quebec small-business deductions for eligible corporations, federal and Quebec research and development incentives where qualifying expenditures exist, and other fact-specific credits. Eligibility depends on ownership, business activity, taxable capital, employee-hours, expenditure, and other statutory tests. No general tax holiday applies to an ordinary online automotive-parts retailer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through CRA-certified tax preparation software and CRA electronic filing services; paper filing is generally restricted to specified cases. Quebec: CO-17, Corporation Income Tax Return, filed through Revenu Québec's online services using authorized tax software, subject to statutory electronic-filing requirements.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax returns. Corporate tax instalments may be required monthly or quarterly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File the T2 and CO-17 within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end. A balance owing is generally due two months after year-end; qualifying CCPCs may have three months to pay if statutory conditions are met. Instalment obligations are separate. A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada generally files a T2; Quebec filing is required where the corporation is subject to Quebec tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Identification and taxation-year fields; CO-17 identification fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the legal name, business number, Quebec identification number where applicable, taxation-year start and end dates, address, incorporation jurisdiction, and principal business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the non-resident corporation accurately and disclose its Canadian business activity and Canadian permanent-establishment information where requested. A non-resident carrying on business in Canada may have a Canadian filing obligation even if it claims treaty protection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 1; CO-17 income and deduction sections
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile net income or loss per financial statements to income for tax purposes, including tax adjustments, deductible expenses, reserves, and capital cost allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income attributable to the Canadian business or permanent establishment under applicable Canadian law and any treaty. Maintain support for deductions, allocations, and foreign head-office charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 5; CO-17 Quebec allocation and tax-calculation sections
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocate taxable income among jurisdictions under applicable allocation rules and calculate federal and Quebec tax, rates, deductions, and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only the income and taxable capital required under the applicable rules. Apply treaty relief through the relevant claim and supporting records; treaty entitlement does not itself eliminate the return-filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 50 and related shareholder disclosures; CO-17 related-party disclosures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report required shareholder, ownership, and related-party information, including transactions and balances where the forms require disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose non-resident shareholders and related-party dealings as required. Assess separate information-return obligations for cross-border transactions, including T106 and country-by-country reporting where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 tax payable and instalment fields; CO-17 tax payable and instalment fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxes, refundable credits, instalments, balances due, and any applicable interest or penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Canadian withholding, instalments, and tax payments to the corporation's assessed liability. Canadian Part XIII withholding on passive payments is a separate obligation from corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: For a late federal T2 return with tax owing, the ordinary penalty is generally 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% for each complete month late, up to 12 months. Enhanced repeat-failure penalties may apply, generally 10% plus 2% per complete month, up to 20 months, where statutory conditions are met. Quebec imposes late-filing penalties and interest under its legislation; amounts depend on the circumstances and duration of default. Failure to file required information returns, including T106, may attract separate penalties. Interest accrues on unpaid tax and may be compounded under applicable rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The Canadian domestic Part XIII withholding rate on dividends paid or credited to a non-resident is generally 25% of the gross amount. An applicable tax treaty may reduce the rate, commonly to 15% or 5% for qualifying corporate shareholders meeting ownership conditions; the precise rate depends on the treaty, beneficial ownership, and any limitation provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before applying a reduced rate, the Canadian payer should obtain and retain appropriate evidence of the recipient's residence and treaty entitlement, commonly CRA Form NR301 for a beneficial owner, or NR302/NR303 for specified intermediary or partnership situations. A certificate of residence from the foreign tax authority may support the claim. The payer must exercise reasonable diligence, retain records, withhold at the domestic rate if entitlement is not adequately established, and remit and report withholding on the applicable schedule. A recipient may seek a refund by filing the appropriate Canadian refund claim. Treaty relief does not remove separate corporate return or transfer-pricing obligations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Part XIII rate is generally 25% on gross royalties paid or credited to a non-resident, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty reductions. Treaty royalty rates vary by treaty and type of royalty and can be zero, reduced, or subject to specific exclusions. Interest paid to an arm's-length non-resident is generally exempt from Canadian withholding, subject to statutory exceptions, including certain participating debt interest and non-arm's-length interest; non-exempt interest is generally subject to 25% domestic withholding, reducible under an applicable treaty. Determine characterization, beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, and any hybrid or back-to-back financing rules before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada has no general CAD threshold that exempts cross-border non-arm's-length transactions from the arm's-length rule or contemporaneous-documentation requirement. Under Income Tax Act section 247, contemporaneous documentation is generally required for relevant transactions with non-residents. The specific transfer-pricing penalty threshold includes an adjustment exceeding the lesser of 10% of gross revenue and CAD 5 million, subject to statutory conditions. Canada does not impose a general OECD-style Master File and Local File submission regime; specified large multinational groups may have country-by-country reporting obligations, generally where consolidated group revenue meets the CAD 1 billion threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no general standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Canadian tax results remain subject to transfer-pricing rules, treaty anti-abuse provisions, the general anti-avoidance rule, beneficial-ownership principles, sham doctrine, and applicable specific anti-avoidance rules. A corporation must maintain genuine commercial records and support its functions, assets, risks, and intercompany charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion, false statements, or wilful failure to comply
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating income, fabricating expenses, concealing taxable activity, making false statements, or wilfully evading Canadian tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil tax reassessment, interest, and penalties may apply. Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act can result in fines of 50% to 200% of tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment for up to five years; indictable offences may carry imprisonment of up to 14 years, depending on the offence and circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for corporate income tax solely by reason of office. Personal criminal liability may arise for directors who participate in or authorize an offence. Director-liability provisions may apply to specified source deductions and other statutory remittances. Civil or criminal consequences depend on the evidence and statutory basis; travel restrictions are not an automatic tax penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing cross-border related-party transactions other than at arm's length, failing to provide required contemporaneous documentation, or failing to make required information returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may adjust income and impose a transfer-pricing penalty generally equal to 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment where statutory thresholds and conditions are met, in addition to tax and interest. Separate information-return penalties may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate reassessments and transfer-pricing penalties are generally imposed on the corporation. Directors may face personal exposure for participation in tax offences or under a specific statutory liability provision; veil piercing is not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold or remit non-resident tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or other taxable amounts to non-residents without required withholding, remittance, reporting, or adequate support for a treaty-reduced rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be liable for unremitted Part XIII tax, interest, and penalties, including penalties for failure to deduct or remit and failure to file required information returns. Treaty relief is not available solely on the basis of a recipient's unsupported assertion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director liability depends on the applicable statutory provision and the director's due-diligence defence. Personal liability is not automatic; criminal liability requires the relevant offence and proof.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the T2, CO-17, T106, or another required return or information return, or filing materially incomplete or inaccurate information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing penalties, information-return penalties, reassessment, and interest may apply. Persistent non-compliance can result in collection action and prosecution where statutory elements are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal consequences only under applicable statutory provisions or for their own participation in an offence. Corporate tax debts do not generally become directors' personal debts merely because they are directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, proceeds of crime, or sanctions evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly dealing with proceeds of crime, disguising beneficial ownership, structuring transactions to conceal source or destination of funds, or dealing with prohibited persons or property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Criminal Code and applicable sanctions legislation may impose asset forfeiture, substantial fines, and imprisonment; specific penalties depend on the offence and conduct. Reporting entities may also face regulatory penalties for breaches of applicable AML obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who authorize, direct, or participate in an offence may face personal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, and asset forfeiture. Travel restrictions may result from criminal process or sanctions measures but are not an automatic corporate tax consequence.
